title: Test case: PICALM (ANTH) orchestration and productive-pit verdict
question: PICALM recruited to the membrane — can it support productive pit formation?

protein.name: PICALM
protein.role: size/regularity setter (Kaksonen); amphipathic ANTH wedge gives dome-level autonomous curvature

method: Ran PICALM's family-screen autonomous curvature as the wedge c_eff through the validated forward model (ccs_curvature), across a SINGLE-VARIABLE-PER-STEP assembly ladder; read the dome/Omega stage vs the Omega/scission boundary. No force point-estimate.
verdict: NO -- PICALM cannot support a productive pit alone (autonomous P(cross Omega)=0.005; alone/coat/coat+actin40 all stay flat, sub-threshold). Isolating the confound: adding the crowding partner (epsin IDP brush) at FIXED 40 pN actin reaches only the dome stage (0.025, not productive), and raising actin to 80 pN reaches Omega ONLY with crowding present. Neither the crowding partner nor the higher force alone is sufficient at these magnitudes -- BOTH are required. This matches the division of labour: PICALM sets vesicle size; epsin/crowding plus actin force together drive productive curvature.
caveat: Forward-model stage call using published/derived c_eff magnitudes, not an inverse on a measured curvature trajectory. The crowding partner contribution (epsin IDP brush c~0.025) is a representative co-player magnitude, not a measurement of this specific assembly.
confound_note: The final productive rung differs from the sub-threshold rungs in TWO factors relative to '+actin 40' (crowding partner AND actin 40->80). The ladder isolates each: crowding-at-40 = 0.025 dome (not productive), so the Omega crossing requires both, not crowding alone.
